items.title: Openness of the flat locus for a finite type module over a locally finitely presented morphism without Noetherian hypotheses
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem is the non Noetherian form of openness of flatness: for a locally finitely presented morphism and a finite type module, provided the weakly associated points of the base are locally finite, the flat locus is open and the module restricts there to a finitely presented flat module (statement lines 4096-4112, tag 05IK). The proof is a real construction: it manufactures a finitely presented model of the stalk that maps to the module, makes it flat over the base and the map surjective after shrinking, bounds the weakly associated points of that model by the weakly associated points of the base times the associated points of the fibres, shrinks the source so that those points specialize into the chosen point, and then shows the kernel vanishes because its weakly associated points would have to be empty. The weakly associated point bookkeeping is the substance, so the claim is H2.
